dispositions.method: Round two of 1799. The sweep check of 24 and 25 November 2026 (X-THIN-SWEEP; outputs/story_discovery_1779/sweep_check_25nov.md) read every passage of the 1799 pages shared word for word by 4 or more papers that no counted opening of round one explains, looked each up in the year's lists and counted it by its own opening words against every page of the year in both transcriptions. It found four items printed by every paper that survives for their weeks (the weeks of July to October, when four papers survive, X-1799-01), which round one's lists did not name; asked, the owner chose on 25 November 2026 to admit them as the rule reads. Every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/round2.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md; verdicts in scan_verdicts/round2*.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As in round one (Y-THIN as amended, B1, and X-1799-01): an item printed by every newspaper that survives for its weeks is admitted; single paragraphs from runs of news are counted by their own words (C-09). Each of the four is printed by all 4 papers of its weeks.

counted_item_by_item.The plundered treasures: 4 of the 4 papers that survive for its weeks (GUS 6 August, PG 12 August, NHG 13 August, PJ 14 August), counted by its own words; the Portland Gazette and the New Hampshire Gazette end the sentence at 'the Austrians', without 'at Parma', and the Providence Journal prints 'at Parmo'.
counted_item_by_item.Milan, 12 June: 4 of 4 (GUS and PG 26 August, NHG 27 August, PJ 28 August), counted by its own opening; a dated paragraph of the Milan news after the paragraph on General Bellegarde (admitted in round one); the Portland Gazette's page is read in its CA transcription, which garbles it.
counted_item_by_item.Verona, 14 June: 4 of 4 on the same pages, counted by its own opening; the New Hampshire Gazette and the Providence Journal print 'has repulsed General Ott, who is now collecting' where the Gazette of the United States has 'has repulsed him. General Otto is now collecting', and the Portland Gazette prints the paragraph abridged (C-02).
counted_item_by_item.Mr. Adams: 4 of 4 (PG 30 September, NHG 1 October, GUS 2 October, PJ 9 October), counted by its own words; in the Portland Gazette the sentence closes a Boston summary of the London news to 12 August (a digest, C-09) and is counted as a printing of the sentence; in the other three it is a paragraph of its own.
